Communication protocols at a glance

A serial protocol sends data one bit after the other over a few wires. Protocols differ in how the receiver knows when a bit is valid (an agreed speed - asynchronous - or a clock line - synchronous), in how many devices share the wires, in how far and how fast they go, and in how errors are found.

UART - Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter

The simplest serial link: every character travels on its own, framed by a start bit and one or more stop bits. There is no clock wire: transmitter and receiver agree on the baud rate (bits per second) and the receiver times the bits from the falling edge of the start bit, sampling each bit in its middle. A difference of about ±2% between the two clocks is tolerated (the error adds up over the 10 bits of a frame).

Signals

SignalDirectionNeededMeaning
TXoutminimumtransmitted data
GND-minimumcommon reference
RXinto receivereceived data (TX of the other side, crossed)
RTS / CTSout / inoptionalhardware flow control: "I can receive" handshake
DTR / DSR, DCD, RIout / inoptionalmodem lines: terminal ready, set ready, carrier detect, ring indicator

Minimum: 2 wires (TX + GND) to send only, 3 (TX, RX, GND) for both directions. Maximum: the 8 signals + GND of a DE-9 connector.

Frame

idle (1) | start (0) | 5-9 data bits, least significant first | parity (optional) | 1, 1.5 or 2 stop bits (1) | idle

  • Data bits: 5 to 9; 8 is by far the most common. "8N1" = 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit: 10 bit times per byte.
  • Parity: odd (the number of ones, parity included, is odd), even, mark (always 1), space (always 0) or none. It finds one wrong bit, not two.
  • Stop bits: the line goes back to idle for at least 1, 1.5 or 2 bit times, so the next start bit can be seen.
  • 9th bit: with 9 data bits the last one often marks an address byte (multiprocessor / multidrop mode).
  • Break: the line held low for longer than a whole frame - used as a reset or a frame marker (LIN, DMX512).

Levels, speeds, distance

TTL / CMOS: idle and 1 = VCC (5 V, 3.3 V or 1.8 V), 0 = 0 V. Usual rates: 300, 1200, 2400, 4800, 9600, 19200, 38400, 57600, 115200, 230400, 460800, 921600 bit/s and more. One bit lasts 1 / baud (104.17 µs at 9600). With 8N1 9600 bit/s carry 960 bytes/s. Distance: from centimetres to a couple of metres - for longer links RS-232, RS-422 or RS-485 transceivers carry the same frame.

The simulator starts from the settings of the port the bytes come from (in the Byte Analyzer). Try parity and 2 stop bits, 7 data bits, MSB first or the 9th bit to see how the frame changes.

UART - Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter

Il collegamento seriale più semplice: ogni carattere viaggia da solo, racchiuso tra un bit di start e uno o più bit di stop. Non c'è un filo di clock: trasmettitore e ricevitore concordano la velocità in baud (bit al secondo) e il ricevitore misura i bit a partire dal fronte di discesa del bit di start, campionando ogni bit a metà. È tollerata una differenza di circa ±2% tra i due clock (l'errore si somma sui 10 bit di un frame).

Minimo: 2 fili (TX + GND) per sola trasmissione, 3 (TX, RX, GND) per le due direzioni. Massimo: gli 8 segnali + GND di un connettore DE-9.

Frame

riposo (1) | start (0) | 5-9 bit di dati, prima il meno significativo | parità (opzionale) | 1, 1,5 o 2 bit di stop (1) | riposo

  • Bit di dati: da 5 a 9; 8 è di gran lunga il più comune. "8N1" = 8 bit di dati, nessuna parità, 1 bit di stop: 10 tempi di bit per byte.
  • Parità: dispari (il numero di uni, parità compresa, è dispari), pari, mark (sempre 1), space (sempre 0) o nessuna. Rileva un bit sbagliato, non due.
  • Bit di stop: la linea torna a riposo per almeno 1, 1,5 o 2 tempi di bit, così il bit di start successivo si vede.
  • 9° bit: con 9 bit di dati l'ultimo spesso indica un byte di indirizzo (modo multiprocessore / multidrop).
  • Break: la linea tenuta bassa per più di un frame intero - usato come reset o come marcatore di frame (LIN, DMX512).

Livelli, velocità, distanza

TTL / CMOS: riposo e 1 = VCC (5 V, 3,3 V o 1,8 V), 0 = 0 V. Velocità usuali: 300, 1200, 2400, 4800, 9600, 19200, 38400, 57600, 115200, 230400, 460800, 921600 bit/s e oltre. Un bit dura 1 / baud (104,17 µs a 9600). Con 8N1, 9600 bit/s trasportano 960 byte/s. Distanza: da pochi centimetri a un paio di metri - per collegamenti più lunghi i transceiver RS-232, RS-422 o RS-485 portano lo stesso frame.

Il simulatore parte dalle impostazioni della porta da cui provengono i byte (nell'Analizzatore di byte). Prova parità e 2 bit di stop, 7 bit di dati, prima il bit più significativo o il 9° bit per vedere come cambia il frame.

RS-232 (TIA-232-F, ITU-T V.24 / V.28)

The classic COM port of the PC. The frame is the UART one, but the voltages are bipolar and inverted, referred to ground: a logic 1 (mark, the idle state) is a negative voltage (-3 to -15 V), a logic 0 (space) is positive (+3 to +15 V). Between -3 and +3 V the level is undefined. Common drivers (MAX232 family) give about ±5 to ±9 V.

Signals (DE-9 connector of the computer, DTE)

4 / 6DTR / DSR - data terminal ready / data set readyout / inoptional

Minimum: 3 wires (TxD, RxD, GND), crossed between two computers (null modem: TxD to RxD). Maximum: 9 pins (DE-9) or 25 (DB-25, which adds a secondary channel and the timing signals of synchronous modems).

Limits

  • Point to point: one driver and one receiver per line.
  • Distance: 15 m (50 ft) by the standard at 19.2 kbit/s (up to 2500 pF of cable); less at higher speeds.
  • Speed: 20 kbit/s by the standard; modern transceivers reach 115.2 kbit/s - 1 Mbit/s.
  • Single-ended and referred to ground: sensitive to noise and ground differences. In plants use RS-422 / RS-485.

The simulation draws the wire as an oscilloscope shows it: idle low (negative), start bit high (positive). The bit values written over the trace are the logical ones.

Il frame è quello UART, ma le tensioni sono bipolari e invertite, riferite a massa: un 1 logico (mark, lo stato di riposo) è una tensione negativa (da -3 a -15 V), uno 0 logico (space) è positivo (da +3 a +15 V). RS-422 (TIA/EIA-422-B)

A differential line: every signal travels on a twisted pair and the receiver looks only at the difference between the two wires, so the noise picked up by both cancels out. The frame is still the UART one. A 1 (mark) is Y (+) above Z (-); the driver gives 2 to 6 V of difference, the receiver needs only 200 mV.

Signals

SignalNeededMeaning
TX+ / TX- (Y / Z)minimumtransmit pair
GNDrecommendedcommon reference (common mode within ±7 V)
RX+ / RX- (A / B)to receivereceive pair (full duplex)
RTS+/-, CTS+/-optionalhandshake on two more pairs

Minimum: one pair + ground (one direction). Usual: two pairs + ground (full duplex, 5 wires). Maximum: four pairs with handshake.

Limits

  • One driver and up to 10 receivers on a pair (multidrop, not multi-master).
  • Up to 10 Mbit/s at 12 m; 1200 m (4000 ft) at about 100 kbit/s - roughly speed x length < 108.
  • Termination: a resistor equal to the cable impedance (100-120 Ω) at the far end of long lines.

The names A/B, +/- and Y/Z are not used the same way by all manufacturers: if nothing is received, swap the two wires of the pair.

RS-485 (TIA/EIA-485-A, ISO/IEC 8482)

Differential like RS-422, but multipoint: many transceivers share one twisted pair and each of them can transmit, one at a time (half duplex). A node enables its driver (DE) only while it sends and listens the rest of the time. The frame is the UART one; protocols such as Modbus RTU, Profibus DP, DMX512 and BACnet MS/TP run on it.

Signals

SignalNeededMeaning
B (+) / A (-), also D+ / D-minimumthe bus pair: 1 (mark, idle) = B above A by at least 200 mV
GND (common)recommendedkeeps the common mode within -7 ... +12 V
DE / RE (at the transceiver)localdriver enable / receiver enable, from the UART or the RTS line
second pair (Y / Z)optional4-wire full duplex (master on one pair, slaves on the other)

Minimum: 2 wires + reference (A, B, GND). Maximum: 4 wires + GND (full duplex).

Bus rules

  • Up to 32 unit loads per bus (32 standard transceivers; 128 with 1/4 UL, 256 with 1/8 UL).
  • Up to 10 Mbit/s over short distances, 1200 m at 100 kbit/s.
  • A line (daisy chain), not a star; termination 120 Ω at both ends; fail-safe biasing (pull-up on B, pull-down on A) so the idle bus reads 1 when nobody drives it.
  • Turnaround: release DE right after the last stop bit, or the slave's answer collides with the end of the request.

Example (the starting data): 01 03 00 00 00 01 84 0A = Modbus RTU, slave 1, function 3 (read holding registers), start 0, quantity 1, CRC-16/MODBUS 0x0A84 sent low byte first. Frames are separated by at least 3.5 character times of silence.

RS-485 (TIA/EIA-485-A, ISO/IEC 8482)

Differenziale come RS-422, ma multipunto: molti transceiver condividono un solo doppino e ognuno può trasmettere, uno alla volta (half duplex). Un nodo abilita il suo driver (DE) solo mentre trasmette e ascolta il resto del tempo. Il frame è quello UART; vi funzionano protocolli come Modbus RTU, Profibus DP, DMX512 e BACnet MS/TP.

Regole del bus

  • Fino a 32 carichi unitari per bus (32 transceiver standard; 128 con 1/4 UL, 256 con 1/8 UL).
  • Fino a 10 Mbit/s su brevi distanze, 1200 m a 100 kbit/s.
  • Una linea (daisy chain), non una stella; terminazione da 120 Ω a entrambe le estremità; polarizzazione fail-safe (pull-up su B, pull-down su A) così il bus a riposo legge 1 quando nessuno lo pilota.
  • Inversione: rilascia DE subito dopo l'ultimo bit di stop, altrimenti la risposta dello slave si sovrappone alla fine della richiesta.

Esempio (i dati iniziali): 01 03 00 00 00 01 84 0A = Modbus RTU, slave 1, funzione 3 (lettura holding register), inizio 0, quantità 1, CRC-16/MODBUS 0x0A84 inviato prima il byte basso. I frame sono separati da almeno 3,5 tempi di carattere di silenzio.

SPI - Serial Peripheral Interface

A synchronous bus introduced by Motorola: the master drives a clock (SCLK) and data moves on both data lines at the same time, one bit per clock - two shift registers in a ring. There are no addresses: the master selects a slave with its own chip select (CS, also SS, usually active low). The protocol has no acknowledge and no checksum; 1 to 50 MHz are common, over 100 MHz for quad SPI flash.

I²C - Inter-Integrated Circuit

A two-wire, synchronous, multi-master bus by Philips (now NXP). Both lines are open drain: devices only pull them low and pull-up resistors (1-10 kΩ) bring them high - so many devices can share them, and any device can hold the clock low to slow the master down (clock stretching). Every slave has an address; every byte is followed by an acknowledge bit from the receiver.

Signals

SignalNeededMeaning

SCLminimumserial clock, from the master (slaves may stretch it)
GNDminimumcommon reference
VDD through pull-upsneeded1.8, 3.3 or 5 V

Always 2 signal wires + ground, whatever the number of devices; the limit is the bus capacitance: 400 pF (550 pF in Fast-mode Plus).

Transfer

S | address (7 bits) + R/W | ACK | data byte | ACK | ... | P

  • START (S): SDA falls while SCL is high. STOP (P): SDA rises while SCL is high. Otherwise SDA changes only while SCL is low.
  • Address: 7 bits (0x08-0x77 usable; 0x00-0x07 and 0x78-0x7F are reserved) followed by R/W (0 = write, 1 = read). A 10-bit address starts with 11110 A9 A8 and continues with a second byte.
  • ACK: the receiver pulls SDA low during the 9th clock; high (NACK) means "no such address", "cannot take more" or - from the master while reading - "that was the last byte".
  • Reading a register: write the register address, then a repeated START (Sr), the address again with R = 1, then read.

SMBus and PMBus derive from I²C (10-100 kHz, timeouts, optional PEC: a CRC-8 byte).

A bus by Dallas Semiconductor (then Maxim Integrated, now Analog Devices) that needs one data wire and ground. The line is pulled up by a resistor (about 4.7 kΩ) and the slaves can even take their power from it (parasite power). There is no clock: the master starts every bit by pulling the line low and the length of the low pulse carries the bit. Every device has a unique 64-bit ROM code (family code, 48-bit serial number, CRC-8), so any number of them can share the line. Typical devices: DS18B20 thermometer, iButton, EEPROMs, battery monitors.

CAN - Controller Area Network (ISO 11898)

The vehicle and industrial bus developed by Bosch: a multi-master differential bus where every node can transmit and every node receives everything. There are no addresses: each frame carries an identifier that says what the data is and, at the same time, its priority. Bits are dominant (0) or recessive (1): when two nodes start together, a node that sends recessive and reads dominant has lost the arbitration and stops - the lowest identifier wins without destroying the frame.

Bit stuffing: from SOF to the end of the CRC, after five equal bits the transmitter inserts one of the opposite value (shown as STF and a 0* / 1*), so the receivers stay synchronised; six equal bits there are an error. Other checks: CRC, form (fixed bits), ACK, bit monitoring. A node that finds an error sends an error frame and the frame is sent again.

CAN FD (ISO 11898-1:2015) extends the data field to 64 bytes with a faster data phase (up to 5-8 Mbit/s) and CRC-17 / CRC-21; CAN XL reaches 2048 bytes. The simulator draws classic CAN 2.0 frames: with more than 8 bytes only the first 8 are sent.

Line codes - how bits become levels

Before any protocol, bits have to become voltages on a wire. The choice decides whether the receiver can recover the clock from the data, whether the signal has a DC component (a problem for transformers and long lines) and how much bandwidth it needs.

CodeRuleClock recoveryUsed by
NRZ-L1 = high, 0 = low for the whole bitno: long runs have no edges (start bits or stuffing are needed)UART, RS-232, SPI, CAN
NRZ-Ia 1 changes the level, a 0 keeps itonly with enough ones (bit stuffing)USB (changes on 0), HDLC, 100BASE-FX
Manchester (IEEE 802.3)a change in the middle of every bit: 0 = high to low, 1 = low to highyes, always10BASE-T Ethernet, DALI, RFID
Manchester (G.E. Thomas)the opposite: 1 = high to low, 0 = low to highyesolder texts, some radio links
Differential Manchesteralways a change in the middle; a 0 also changes at the start of the bityes, and wires may be swappedToken Ring (IEEE 802.5); biphase mark (AES3, S/PDIF) is similar
RZa 1 is high for the first half of the bit, then back to zerofor onesinfrared (IrDA uses short pulses), optical links
Bipolar AMI0 = 0 V, the ones alternately +V and -Vwith enough ones (B8ZS / HDB3)T1 / E1 telephone lines

Manchester and its variants need twice the bandwidth of NRZ (an edge every half bit) but have no DC component and carry the clock; NRZ is the most compact and needs framing (start bits, stuffing) to stay synchronised. The simulator draws the clock, the NRZ data as reference and the encoded line.

JTAG - IEEE 1149.1 (Joint Test Action Group)

A synchronous interface built into chips for boundary-scan testing of boards and, by extension, for debugging and programming microcontrollers, processors, FPGAs and CPLDs. Every chip has a Test Access Port (TAP): a 16-state machine driven only by TMS, sampled on the rising edge of TCK. Through it the host selects the instruction register (IR) or a data register (DR) and shifts bits through it - TDI in, TDO out, least significant bit first, one bit per clock.

Signals

SignalDirectionNeededMeaning
TCKhost to deviceminimumtest clock
TMShost to deviceminimumtest mode select: drives the TAP state machine (pulled up)
TDIhost to deviceminimumtest data in (pulled up)
TDOdevice to hostminimumtest data out: changes on the falling edge of TCK, high impedance outside the Shift states
TRST*host to deviceoptionalasynchronous TAP reset, active low
RTCKdevice to hostoptionalreturned clock, for adaptive clocking (ARM cores)
SRST* / nRESETbothoptionalsystem reset of the target (not part of IEEE 1149.1)
VTrefdevice to proberecommendedthe target's I/O voltage, so the probe matches its levels
GND-minimumcommon reference

Minimum: 4 signals (TCK, TMS, TDI, TDO) + GND. Maximum: the 5 TAP signals with TRST*, plus RTCK, SRST*, VTref and GND on the usual connectors (ARM 20-pin 2.54 mm, Cortex debug 10-pin 1.27 mm, TI 14-pin, Xilinx 14-pin). Fewer wires: cJTAG (IEEE 1149.7) on 2 wires TCKC / TMSC, and Arm's SWD (Serial Wire Debug, SWCLK / SWDIO), which is not JTAG but often shares the connector.

TAP state machine

Five clocks with TMS = 1 always reach Test-Logic-Reset, whatever the state. From Run-Test/Idle:

ScanTMSStates
IR scan1 1 0 0, then 0 for every bit but the last, 1, then 1 0Select-DR-Scan, Select-IR-Scan, Capture-IR, Shift-IR (the last bit with TMS = 1 goes to Exit1-IR), Update-IR, Run-Test/Idle
DR scan1 0 0, then 0 for every bit but the last, 1, then 1 0Select-DR-Scan, Capture-DR, Shift-DR, Exit1-DR, Update-DR, Run-Test/Idle

The other states (Pause-IR / Pause-DR, Exit2-IR / Exit2-DR) let the host stop shifting without leaving the scan. Capture loads the register (the IR captures ...01, which helps to find the chain length); Update makes the shifted value take effect.

Instructions and registers

  • BYPASS (IR all ones, mandatory): a 1-bit data register - TDO is TDI one clock later; it shortens a chain to the chips of interest.
  • IDCODE (optional, selected after reset): a 32-bit identification - version, part number, manufacturer (JEDEC code), bit 0 = 1.
  • SAMPLE/PRELOAD, EXTEST (mandatory): read the pins or drive them through the boundary-scan register (one cell per pin) - testing a board without probes.
  • Vendor instructions: debug access (e.g. the ARM debug port), flash and FPGA programming. The chip's BSDL file lists its instructions and the length of its IR.

Chain and speed

Several chips are chained: TCK, TMS (and TRST*) go to all of them, TDI enters chip 1, its TDO feeds TDI of chip 2 ... and the last TDO returns to the host; an IR scan shifts all the instruction registers one after the other. Clocks of 1 to 50 MHz are usual (often 1 - 10 MHz, limited by the slowest chip, the cable and - on ARM cores - the core clock, hence RTCK).

The simulator shows an optional TRST* pulse, the TAP reset, an optional IR scan with the instruction you choose, then a DR scan of the data (LSB first of every byte), with the TAP state of every clock, and TDO as a device in BYPASS (TDI one clock later), all ones, or loopback.

JTAG - IEEE 1149.1 (Joint Test Action Group)

Un'interfaccia sincrona integrata nei chip per il collaudo boundary-scan delle schede e, per estensione, per il debug e la programmazione di microcontrollori, processori, FPGA e CPLD. Ogni chip ha una Test Access Port (TAP): una macchina a 16 stati pilotata solo da TMS, campionato sul fronte di salita di TCK. Attraverso di essa l'host seleziona il registro istruzioni (IR) o un registro dati (DR) e vi fa scorrere i bit - TDI in ingresso, TDO in uscita, prima il bit meno significativo, un bit per clock.

Segnali

SegnaleDirezioneNecessarioSignificato

TMSdall'host al dispositivominimoselezione del modo di test: pilota la macchina a stati TAP (con pull-up)
TDIdall'host al dispositivominimodati di test in ingresso (con pull-up)
TDOdal dispositivo all'hostminimodati di test in uscita: cambia sul fronte di discesa di TCK, in alta impedenza fuori dagli stati Shift
TRST*dall'host al dispositivoopzionalereset asincrono della TAP, attivo basso
RTCKdal dispositivo all'hostopzionaleclock restituito, per il clock adattivo (core ARM)

GND-minimoriferimento comune

Minimo: 4 segnali (TCK, TMS, TDI, TDO) + GND. Massimo: i 5 segnali TAP con TRST*, più RTCK, SRST*, VTref e GND sui connettori usuali (ARM 20 pin passo 2,54 mm, Cortex debug 10 pin passo 1,27 mm, TI 14 pin, Xilinx 14 pin). Con meno fili: cJTAG (IEEE 1149.7) su 2 fili TCKC / TMSC, e l'SWD di Arm (Serial Wire Debug, SWCLK / SWDIO), che non è JTAG ma spesso condivide il connettore.

Macchina a stati TAP

Cinque clock con TMS = 1 portano sempre a Test-Logic-Reset, qualunque sia lo stato. Da Run-Test/Idle:

ScansioneTMSStati
Scansione IR1 1 0 0, poi 0 per ogni bit tranne l'ultimo, 1, poi 1 0Select-DR-Scan, Select-IR-Scan, Capture-IR, Shift-IR (l'ultimo bit con TMS = 1 porta a Exit1-IR), Update-IR, Run-Test/Idle
Scansione DR1 0 0, poi 0 per ogni bit tranne l'ultimo, 1, poi 1 0Select-DR-Scan, Capture-DR, Shift-DR, Exit1-DR, Update-DR, Run-Test/Idle

Gli altri stati (Pause-IR / Pause-DR, Exit2-IR / Exit2-DR) permettono all'host di fermare lo scorrimento senza uscire dalla scansione. Capture carica il registro (l'IR cattura ...01, utile per trovare la lunghezza della catena); Update rende effettivo il valore fatto scorrere.

Istruzioni e registri

  • BYPASS (IR tutto a uno, obbligatoria): un registro dati di 1 bit - TDO è TDI un clock dopo; accorcia una catena ai soli chip di interesse.
  • IDCODE (opzionale, selezionata dopo il reset): un'identificazione di 32 bit - versione, codice del componente, costruttore (codice JEDEC), bit 0 = 1.
  • SAMPLE/PRELOAD, EXTEST (obbligatorie): leggono i pin o li pilotano attraverso il registro boundary-scan (una cella per pin) - collaudo di una scheda senza sonde.
  • Istruzioni del costruttore: accesso di debug (es. la porta di debug ARM), programmazione di flash e FPGA. Il file BSDL del chip elenca le sue istruzioni e la lunghezza del suo IR.

Catena e velocità

Più chip si collegano in catena: TCK, TMS (e TRST*) vanno a tutti, TDI entra nel chip 1, il suo TDO alimenta il TDI del chip 2 ... e l'ultimo TDO torna all'host; una scansione IR fa scorrere tutti i registri istruzioni uno dopo l'altro. Sono usuali clock da 1 a 50 MHz (spesso 1 - 10 MHz, limitati dal chip più lento, dal cavo e - sui core ARM - dal clock del core, da cui RTCK).

Il simulatore mostra un impulso TRST* opzionale, il reset della TAP, una scansione IR opzionale con l'istruzione scelta, poi una scansione DR dei dati (prima il bit meno significativo di ogni byte), con lo stato TAP di ogni clock, e TDO come un dispositivo in BYPASS (TDI un clock dopo), tutto a uno, o loopback.

protocol "Name" a protocol; its lines up to "end" sync AA 55 the frame starts with these bytes (hex) end 0D 0A the frame ends with these bytes length 12 every frame has 12 bytes, or: length field len + 6 the whole frame is the value of field len + 6 bytes (also * N, - N) order little numbers without le / be are little-endian (default: big) checksum CRC-16/MODBUS from 0 to -3 at -2 little any CRC or sum of the Byte Analyzer, by name; over the bytes from .. to (negative: counted from the end, -1 = the last byte), the value at "at" match addr == 1 the frame is this protocol only if the condition holds field NAME TYPE OPTIONS the fields in order when cmd == 0x81 the fields up to "end" exist only in that case (also != < > <= >= in 1,2,3) field ... end end
Types: u8 i8 u16 i16 u24 i24 u32 i32 u64 i64 f32 f64 - add le or be for the byte order (u16le) bytes N | bytes FIELD | bytes * N bytes, as many as a field before says, or the rest text N | text FIELD | text * | text zero characters (zero: up to a 00 byte) bcd N N bytes of BCD digits Options: scale 0.1 offset -40 unit "C" hex hidden enum 1=Read 2=Write 0x81="Read reply" names of the values bits 0=ready 1=error 2-3=mode names of bits (a range shows its value)
Without sync, length and end a protocol takes the whole message as it arrives (the receive options of the tab cut the messages). With sync and length or end it also finds frames inside a message and cuts them from a stream (the plotter). A frame with a wrong checksum is shown as WRONG. entry.key:
Data are Lua strings of bytes ("\x02AT\r" or spm.bytes("02 41 54 0D")). string.pack / string.unpack read and write numbers: string.unpack("<i2", data, 3).
Sending and printing spm.send(data) send bytes on the port (true if sent) spm.sendhex("AA 55 01") the same, written in hex spm.log(...) print(...) a line in the output (or in the tab's console for a hook) spm.hex(data [, sep]) "AA 55 01" spm.bytes("AA 55") -> data spm.crc("CRC-16/MODBUS", data) any CRC or sum of the Byte Analyzer, by name -> number spm.decode(data [, protocol]) the frames of the protocol definitions: { {protocol=, ok=, summary=, values={temp=21.5, ...}}, ... } spm.time() milliseconds (for durations)
Waiting (only in scripts run from Tools > Lua Scripts or --lua; the program keeps working) spm.wait(ms) spm.receive(timeout) what arrived (waits for it) -> data, or nil after timeout ms spm.expect("OK", timeout) true when the text arrives, false after timeout ms spm.expect_match("T=(%d+)", t) a Lua pattern: its captures (or the match), nil after t ms spm.flush() forget what was received so far
Results spm.check(condition, "text") PASS or FAIL, counted spm.pass("text") spm.fail("text") The run ends PASSED (all checks passed), FAILED, with an ERROR (its line) or STOPPED. 20 million instructions without a wait stop the script (an endless loop).
Hooks (console right-click > Lua hook: a script loaded into the tab) function on_receive(data) ... end every message received function on_send(data) return ... end the Send button: a string = send that instead, false = send nothing, nil = unchanged spm.every(ms, function() ... end) repeatedly
library.lua (read at the start and by Apply) spm.dissector("Name", function(data) return { {"temp", 21.5, unit="C"}, ... } end) decodes messages in the console, the Line Monitor and the plotter; nil = not its message; a field: {name, value, unit=, offset=, size=, hidden=true}; also checksum="...", ok=false spm.plotter("Name", function(data) return { temp = 21.5, hum = 40 } end) the plotter's "Values from: Lua: Name"
Lua itself: https://www.lua.org/manual/5.4/

I dati sono stringhe Lua di byte ("\x02AT\r" o spm.bytes("02 41 54 0D")). string.pack / string.unpack leggono e scrivono numeri: string.unpack("<i2", data, 3).
Inviare e stampare spm.send(data) invia byte sulla porta (true se inviati) spm.sendhex("AA 55 01") lo stesso, scritto in esadecimale spm.log(...) print(...) una riga nell'output (o nella console della scheda per un hook) spm.hex(data [, sep]) "AA 55 01" spm.bytes("AA 55") -> data spm.crc("CRC-16/MODBUS", data) qualsiasi CRC o somma del Byte Analyzer, per nome -> numero spm.decode(data [, protocol]) i frame delle definizioni di protocollo: { {protocol=, ok=, summary=, values={temp=21.5, ...}}, ... } spm.time() millisecondi (per le durate)
Attendere (solo negli script avviati da Strumenti > Script Lua o --lua; il programma continua a funzionare) spm.wait(ms) spm.receive(timeout) ciò che è arrivato (lo attende) -> data, o nil dopo timeout ms spm.expect("OK", timeout) true quando arriva il testo, false dopo timeout ms spm.expect_match("T=(%d+)", t) un pattern Lua: le sue catture (o la corrispondenza), nil dopo t ms spm.flush() dimentica ciò che è stato ricevuto finora
Risultati spm.check(condizione, "testo") PASS o FAIL, contati spm.pass("testo") spm.fail("testo") L'esecuzione finisce SUPERATO (tutti i controlli superati), FALLITO, con un ERRORE (la sua riga) o FERMATO. 20 milioni di istruzioni senza un'attesa fermano lo script (un ciclo infinito).
Hook (clic destro sulla console > Hook Lua: uno script caricato nella scheda) function on_receive(data) ... end ogni messaggio ricevuto function on_send(data) return ... end il pulsante Invia: una stringa = invia quella, false = non inviare nulla, nil = invariato spm.every(ms, function() ... end) ripetutamente
library.lua (letta all'avvio e con Applica) spm.dissector("Nome", function(data) return { {"temp", 21.5, unit="C"}, ... } end) decodifica i messaggi nella console, nel Monitor di linea e nel plotter; nil = non è suo; un campo: {nome, valore, unit=, offset=, size=, hidden=true}; anche checksum="...", ok=false spm.plotter("Nome", function(data) return { temp = 21.5, hum = 40 } end) i "Valori da: Lua: Nome" del plotter
Il linguaggio Lua: https://www.lua.org/manual/5.4/
